Can Combining Histopathology and RNA-seq Improve Risk Stratification to Reduce Under-treatment in Breast Cancer?

DATA3888 Data Science Capstone, Biomed17

Guanyu Chen, Serafina Aurelia, Kush Dewan, Thinh Duong, Ni Putu Ananda Maheswari, Nael Panjaitan

2026-05-31

1 Executive Summary

Background. Breast cancer treatment decisions in early-stage disease rely on histopathological markers that, while clinically essential, do not fully reflect the molecular heterogeneity of the tumour. Patients whose RNA-seq profile diverges from their histopathological assessment may receive treatment that is mismatched to their underlying biology, with measurable consequences for survival.

Methods. Using the SCAN-B GSE96058 cohort restricted to ER-positive, endocrine-treated patients (n = 2,512), four survival models were compared under a single nested cross-validation framework (5 repeats by 5 outer folds, 25 fits each): Cox proportional hazards with LASSO regularisation in two configurations (gene expression only, and gene expression plus six histopathological variables), and the analogous pair of Random Survival Forest models. Discrimination was measured by Harrell’s C-statistic, with paired t-tests comparing within each model family across identical folds.

Key Findings. The combined Cox model achieved the highest mean C-statistic (0.766, SD 0.036), significantly outperforming the gene-only Cox model (0.695, SD 0.044, paired t-test p < 0.0001). The same pattern held for Random Survival Forest (combined: 0.716, gene-only: 0.674, paired p < 0.0001), but the parametric Cox approach exceeded the non-parametric forest at both configurations. Stability selection identified 11 genes consistently retained by the combined Cox model, and the final refit stratified patients into three risk tiers with sharply separated observed mortality (Low 1.2%, Medium 4.9%, High 20.2%).

Conclusion. Combining histopathology with RNA-seq materially improves survival risk stratification in ER+ endocrine-treated breast cancer. The resulting model is operationalised via a Shiny application that returns a personalised risk tier and per-feature drivers for clinician review.

2 Introduction

Breast cancer is the most common malignancy among women worldwide and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with more than two million new diagnoses each year (Sung et al., 2021). Treatment decisions for early-stage hormone-receptor-positive disease are guided primarily by histopathological and clinicopathological indicators: tumour grade, estrogen and progesterone receptor (ER/PgR) status, HER2 status, Ki67, tumour size, and nodal involvement. These markers are central to current clinical practice but do not fully capture the molecular heterogeneity of breast cancer, leaving open the question of whether some patients are systematically under-treated relative to their underlying risk.

RNA sequencing offers a complementary view of tumour biology by measuring genome-wide gene expression (Kukurba and Montgomery, 2015). Brueffer et al. (2018) demonstrated that RNA-seq based multigene classifiers can approach the accuracy of conventional histopathology for biomarker assessment and improve prognostic stratification in hormone-responsive subtypes. Despite this evidence, a translational gap persists: identifying discordance between molecular and histopathological signal is one task, and turning that signal into a decision-support output that practising clinicians can act on is another.

2.1 Research Question

This project addresses the following question:

Does combining histopathology with RNA-seq expression data improve survival risk stratification in ER-positive, endocrine-treated breast cancer, and can the resulting risk score be translated into clinically actionable tiers?

Three concrete sub-aims follow. First, evaluate whether two distinct modelling families, Cox proportional hazards with LASSO and Random Survival Forest, give consistent answers about the marginal value of histopathological variables on top of gene expression. Second, identify a small, stable gene panel that can be elicited from a single CSV upload in a deployable tool. Third, translate the resulting continuous risk score into a three-tier output (Low, Medium, High) that maps onto a clinical reassessment decision.

3 Background

3.1 Dataset

All analyses use GSE96058 from the SCAN-B (Sweden Cancerome Analysis Network, Breast) study, a population-based cohort of breast tumours profiled by RNA sequencing with linked clinical and histopathological records. The full cohort comprises six expression sub-matrices plus a replicate set. After removing replicates and excluding patients with missing ER status, the working cohort contains 2,512 ER-positive, endocrine-treated patients with overall survival follow-up (ovrallSurvDays, ovrallSurvEvent). Six routine histopathological and clinicopathological variables are used: NHG grade, PgR status, HER2 status, tumour size, age at diagnosis, and lymph node status. Ki67 was excluded due to a 54.8% missingness rate.

3.2 Motivating Evidence

The clinical motivation for combining RNA-seq with histopathology comes from a signal in the SCAN-B data itself. When the molecular ER classifier (er_MGC) disagrees with the histopathological ER call, specifically MGC-negative but Hist-positive (denoted “FN”), overall survival is markedly worse than for fully concordant ER-positive (TP) patients (Figure 1, log-rank p = 0.0017). This indicates that the histopathological label alone misses a clinically meaningful subgroup whose biology is captured by gene expression, providing the empirical justification for the modelling approach that follows.

library(GSE96058)
library(tidyverse)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(glmnet)
library(limma)
library(survcomp)
library(randomForestSRC)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
for (OBJ in data(package = "GSE96058")$results[, "Item"])
  assign(sub("GSE96058_", "", OBJ), get(OBJ))

detach(package:GSE96058, unload = TRUE)

full_expression <- cbind(
  geneExpression_sub1,
  geneExpression_sub2,
  geneExpression_sub3,
  geneExpression_sub4,
  geneExpression_sub5,
  geneExpression_repl1
)

df_full <- sampDesc %>%
  filter(isRepl == FALSE,
         er_Status != "NA")

df_erpos_endo <- df_full %>%
  filter(er_Status == 1,
         endocrine_treated == 1) %>%
  mutate(
    lymphNode_binary = case_when(
      lymphNode_Status == "NodeNegative" ~ 0,
      lymphNode_Status == "NodePositive" ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    lymphNode_binary = ifelse(is.na(lymphNode_binary), 0, lymphNode_binary),
    pgr_Status       = ifelse(is.na(pgr_Status),  1, pgr_Status),
    her2_Status      = ifelse(is.na(her2_Status),  0, her2_Status),
    tumor_size       = ifelse(is.na(tumor_size),
                              median(tumor_size, na.rm = TRUE), tumor_size),
    ovrallSurvEvent  = as.numeric(ovrallSurvEvent)
  )


expr_endo <- full_expression[,
               colnames(full_expression) %in% df_erpos_endo$title,
               drop = FALSE]

df_erpos_endo <- df_erpos_endo[
  match(colnames(expr_endo), df_erpos_endo$title), ]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(expr_endo), df_erpos_endo$title))

saveRDS(df_erpos_endo, "./models/df_erpos_endo.rds")
saveRDS(expr_endo,     "./models/expr_endo.rds")
df_eda <- df_full %>%
  mutate(er_concordance = case_when(
    er_MGC == 0 & er_Status == 0 ~ "TN",
    er_MGC == 1 & er_Status == 1 ~ "TP",
    er_MGC == 0 & er_Status == 1 ~ "FN",
    er_MGC == 1 & er_Status == 0 ~ "FP",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  ))

df_conc <- df_eda %>%
  filter(er_concordance %in% c("FN", "TP")) %>%
  mutate(ovrallSurvEvent = as.numeric(ovrallSurvEvent))
surv_fit_eda <- survfit(Surv(ovrallSurvDays, ovrallSurvEvent) ~ er_concordance,
                        data = df_conc)
ggsurvplot(
  surv_fit_eda, data = df_conc, pval = TRUE,
  legend.title = "ER concordance",
  legend.labs  = c("Discordant (MGC-/Hist+)", "Concordant (TP)"),
  palette      = c("#B02020", "#1B7A4A"),
  xlab         = "Time (days)",
  ylab         = "Overall survival probability",
  risk.table   = FALSE
)

Figure 1. Kaplan-Meier overall survival in the SCAN-B cohort, comparing fully concordant ER-positive (TP) patients to MGC-negative / Hist-positive discordant (FN) patients. The log-rank test gives p = 0.0017, indicating that the discordant subgroup has significantly worse survival than the fully concordant group. This is the empirical motivation for combining RNA-seq with histopathology.

4 Methods

4.1 Workflow Overview

Figure 2 summarises the end-to-end pipeline: cohort selection from GSE96058, nested cross-validation across Cox-LASSO and Random Survival Forest (each in gene-only and combined configurations), aggregation of C-statistics, final refit with tertile cutoffs, and deployment as a risk analysis tool. Yellow boxes denote data steps, blue boxes compute steps, and green the final deliverable.

knitr::include_graphics("workflow_diagram.png")

Figure 2. Analysis workflow for Cox-LASSO and Random Survival Forest model development. Yellow = data processes, blue = compute processes, green = deliverables. The nested cross-validation block (5 outer x 5 inner folds) evaluates both model families in parallel before the highest-performing configuration is selected for the final risk analysis tool.

4.2 Data Preprocessing

The six expression sub-matrices supplied with the GSE96058 R data package were concatenated into a single gene-by-sample expression matrix and aligned with the clinical metadata. Replicate samples were dropped, missing categorical clinical values were imputed by mode (lymph node negative for missing nodal status, PgR-positive and HER2-negative defaults for missing receptor calls), and tumour size was median-imputed. The cohort was then restricted to ER-positive patients on endocrine therapy. Overall survival was modelled in days with the associated event indicator; no other endpoints (e.g. disease-free survival) were considered in this analysis. The full data assembly code is shown in the data-load chunk earlier in the report.

4.3 Modelling Framework

Four candidate models were evaluated under a single nested cross-validation design, two from each modelling family:

  • Cox-Gene: Cox proportional hazards with LASSO regularisation (glmnet, family = "cox", alpha = 1), gene-expression features only.
  • Cox-Combined: Cox proportional hazards with LASSO, gene expression plus six histopathological variables; clinical variables entered with penalty.factor = 0 so they were always retained while gene coefficients were subject to L1 shrinkage.
  • RSF-Gene: Random Survival Forest (randomForestSRC::rfsrc), gene-expression features only.
  • RSF-Combined: Random Survival Forest with the six histopathological variables added.

Cox-LASSO and Random Survival Forest sit at opposite ends of the bias-variance trade-off for survival data. Cox-LASSO is semi-parametric, assumes proportional hazards, and yields interpretable per-feature coefficients suitable for clinical deployment (Friedman et al., 2010). RSF is non-parametric, makes no proportional-hazards assumption, and captures non-linearities and interactions automatically (Ishwaran et al., 2008). Running both families across the same outer folds lets us check whether the conclusion about the marginal value of histopathological variables is an artefact of one model class or a genuine signal in the data.

4.4 Nested Cross-Validation

All four models share the same 5 repeats by 5-fold outer cross-validation (25 outer fits), stratified on event status, with an inner 5-fold loop used for feature selection and hyperparameter tuning. For each outer fold, approximately 2,010 patients form the outer training set and 502 form the held-out outer test set.

Supervised gene selection is identical across all four models. Within each inner training fold, a variance filter (var > 0.5) removes low-signal probes, followed by limma differential expression (event vs no event, BH-adjusted p < 0.05) to retain genes associated with survival. The union of significant genes across the five inner folds forms the candidate set passed to the outer training. The union (rather than intersection) was chosen to maximise coverage of marginally informative genes; the Results section confirms that this does not lead to overfitting.

For Cox-LASSO, the inner CV is also used to select the regularisation parameter via cv.glmnet at lambda.min. For RSF, the inner CV selects ntree from {500, 1000}, with nodesize fixed at 15 and variable importance enabled on the outer fit. After the inner loop completes, limma is rerun on the full outer training set and the final outer-fold model is fit at the inner-CV-selected hyperparameter.

var_thresh      <- 0.5
pval_thresh     <- 0.05
n_outer_repeats <- 5
n_outer_folds   <- 5
n_inner_folds   <- 5

histopath_vars <- c("nhg", "pgr_Status", "her2_Status",
                    "tumor_size", "ageAtDx", "lymphNode_binary")

make_stratified_folds <- function(y, nfolds, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  fold_id <- integer(length(y))
  for (cls in unique(y)) {
    idx <- which(y == cls)
    fold_id[idx] <- sample(rep(seq_len(nfolds), length.out = length(idx)))
  }
  fold_id
}

select_genes_limma <- function(expr_train, event_train,
                               var_thresh, pval_thresh) {
  gv     <- apply(expr_train, 1, var)
  keep_v <- rownames(expr_train)[gv > var_thresh]
  if (length(keep_v) < 2) return(character(0))
  expr_v <- expr_train[keep_v, , drop = FALSE]
  if (length(unique(event_train)) < 2) return(character(0))
  design <- model.matrix(~ event_train)
  fit    <- eBayes(lmFit(expr_v, design))
  tt     <- topTable(fit, coef = 2, number = Inf,
                     adjust.method = "BH", sort.by = "p")
  rownames(tt)[tt$adj.P.Val < pval_thresh]
}

n_outer_total <- n_outer_repeats * n_outer_folds

cox_rds_path <- "./models/cox_m2_m3_final.rds"
rsf_rds_path <- "./models/rsf_nested_cv.rds"

cox_cv_in_memory <- function() {
  exists("c_model2", inherits = FALSE) &&
    exists("c_model3", inherits = FALSE) &&
    length(c_model2) == n_outer_total &&
    any(!is.na(c_model2))
}

rsf_cv_in_memory <- function() {
  exists("c_rsf_genes", inherits = FALSE) &&
    exists("c_rsf_combined", inherits = FALSE) &&
    length(c_rsf_genes) == n_outer_total &&
    any(!is.na(c_rsf_genes))
}
compute_c <- function(lp, surv_time, surv_event) {
  tryCatch(
    concordance.index(
      x          = lp,
      surv.time  = surv_time,
      surv.event = surv_event,
      method     = "noether"
    )$c.index,
    error = function(e) NA_real_
  )
}

cox_results_ready <- cox_cv_in_memory()

if (!cox_results_ready && file.exists(cox_rds_path)) {
  saved <- readRDS(cox_rds_path)
  c_model2            <- saved$c_model2
  c_model3            <- saved$c_model3
  fold_summary_cox    <- saved$fold_summary
  selection_counts_m2 <- saved$selection_counts_m2
  selection_counts_m3 <- saved$selection_counts_m3
  coef_sums_m2        <- saved$coef_sums_m2
  coef_sums_m3        <- saved$coef_sums_m3
  cox_results_ready   <- TRUE
  cat("Cox nested-CV results loaded from", cox_rds_path, "\n")
} else if (cox_results_ready) {
  cat("Cox nested-CV results already in memory; skipping recompute.\n")
}
if (!cox_results_ready) {
  c_model2 <- numeric(n_outer_total)
  c_model3 <- numeric(n_outer_total)

  fold_log <- vector("list", n_outer_total)
  fit_i    <- 0L

  selection_counts_m2 <- integer(0)
  coef_sums_m2        <- numeric(0)
  selection_counts_m3 <- integer(0)
  coef_sums_m3        <- numeric(0)
}
# Cox nested CV.
# Internal naming uses model2 (gene only) and model3 (combined), as in
# the original cox_models.Rmd; in the report these are referred to as
# Cox-Gene and Cox-Combined respectively.
# Skips the loop when results are already in memory or in cox_rds_path.

if (cox_results_ready) {
  cat("Skipping Cox nested-CV loop (using saved results).\n")
} else {

for (rep_i in seq_len(n_outer_repeats)) {

  cat("=== Repeat", rep_i, "===\n")

  outer_folds <- make_stratified_folds(
    df_erpos_endo$ovrallSurvEvent,
    n_outer_folds,
    seed = 2000 + rep_i
  )

  for (k in seq_len(n_outer_folds)) {

    fit_i  <- fit_i + 1L
    tr_idx <- which(outer_folds != k)
    te_idx <- which(outer_folds == k)

    train_df   <- df_erpos_endo[tr_idx, ]
    test_df    <- df_erpos_endo[te_idx, ]
    train_surv <- Surv(train_df$ovrallSurvDays, train_df$ovrallSurvEvent)
    expr_tr    <- expr_endo[, tr_idx, drop = FALSE]
    expr_te    <- expr_endo[, te_idx, drop = FALSE]

    cat("  Fold", k,
        "| train:", length(tr_idx),
        "| test:",  length(te_idx), "\n")

    inner_folds <- make_stratified_folds(
      train_df$ovrallSurvEvent,
      n_inner_folds,
      seed = 5000 + 100 * rep_i + k
    )

    candidate_genes_inner <- vector("list", n_inner_folds)

    for (ik in seq_len(n_inner_folds)) {
      itr_idx   <- which(inner_folds != ik)
      expr_itr  <- expr_tr[, itr_idx, drop = FALSE]
      event_itr <- train_df$ovrallSurvEvent[itr_idx]
      candidate_genes_inner[[ik]] <- select_genes_limma(
        expr_itr, event_itr, var_thresh, pval_thresh
      )
    }

    union_genes <- unique(unlist(candidate_genes_inner))
    union_genes <- union_genes[nchar(union_genes) > 0]

    cat("    Inner union genes:", length(union_genes), "\n")

    if (length(union_genes) < 2) {
      cat("    Too few genes, skipping M2 and M3\n")
      c_model2[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      c_model3[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      next
    }

    x_tr_inner <- t(expr_tr[union_genes, , drop = FALSE])

    cv_inner <- cv.glmnet(
      x        = x_tr_inner,
      y        = train_surv,
      family   = "cox",
      alpha    = 1,
      foldid   = inner_folds,
      cox.ties = "breslow"
    )

    best_lambda_m2 <- cv_inner$lambda.min
    best_lambda_m3 <- cv_inner$lambda.min

    outer_genes <- select_genes_limma(
      expr_tr, train_df$ovrallSurvEvent,
      var_thresh, pval_thresh
    )

    cat("    Outer DGE genes:", length(outer_genes), "\n")

    if (length(outer_genes) < 2) {
      cat("    Too few outer genes, skipping\n")
      c_model2[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      c_model3[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      next
    }

    x_tr_outer <- t(expr_tr[outer_genes, , drop = FALSE])
    x_te_outer <- t(expr_te[outer_genes, , drop = FALSE])

    final_m2 <- glmnet(
      x        = x_tr_outer,
      y        = train_surv,
      family   = "cox",
      alpha    = 1,
      lambda   = best_lambda_m2,
      cox.ties = "breslow"
    )

    cox2_pred <- as.vector(
      predict(final_m2, newx = x_te_outer,
              s = best_lambda_m2, type = "link")
    )

    c2 <- compute_c(cox2_pred,
                    test_df$ovrallSurvDays,
                    test_df$ovrallSurvEvent)

    cc2      <- coef(final_m2, s = best_lambda_m2)
    cc2_vals <- setNames(as.numeric(cc2), rownames(cc2))
    nz2      <- names(cc2_vals)[cc2_vals != 0]

    cat("    M2 genes:", length(nz2),
        "| lambda:", round(best_lambda_m2, 4),
        "| C:", round(c2, 3), "\n")

    for (g in nz2) {
      prev_n <- if (g %in% names(selection_counts_m2)) selection_counts_m2[[g]] else 0L
      prev_c <- if (g %in% names(coef_sums_m2))        coef_sums_m2[[g]]        else 0
      selection_counts_m2[g] <- prev_n + 1L
      coef_sums_m2[g]        <- prev_c + cc2_vals[g]
    }

    train_hist_mat <- model.matrix(
      ~ nhg + pgr_Status + her2_Status +
        tumor_size + ageAtDx + lymphNode_binary - 1,
      data = train_df
    )
    test_hist_mat <- model.matrix(
      ~ nhg + pgr_Status + her2_Status +
        tumor_size + ageAtDx + lymphNode_binary - 1,
      data = test_df
    )

    common_cols    <- intersect(colnames(train_hist_mat),
                                colnames(test_hist_mat))
    train_hist_mat <- train_hist_mat[, common_cols, drop = FALSE]
    test_hist_mat  <- test_hist_mat[,  common_cols, drop = FALSE]
    n_hist_cols    <- ncol(train_hist_mat)

    x_tr_outer_m3 <- cbind(train_hist_mat, x_tr_outer)
    x_te_outer_m3 <- cbind(test_hist_mat,  x_te_outer)
    pen_outer_m3  <- c(rep(0, n_hist_cols),
                       rep(1, length(outer_genes)))

    final_m3 <- glmnet(
      x              = x_tr_outer_m3,
      y              = train_surv,
      family         = "cox",
      alpha          = 1,
      lambda         = best_lambda_m3,
      penalty.factor = pen_outer_m3,
      cox.ties       = "breslow"
    )

    cox3_pred <- as.vector(
      predict(final_m3, newx = x_te_outer_m3,
              s = best_lambda_m3, type = "link")
    )

    c3 <- compute_c(cox3_pred,
                    test_df$ovrallSurvDays,
                    test_df$ovrallSurvEvent)

    cc3       <- coef(final_m3, s = best_lambda_m3)
    cc3_vals  <- setNames(as.numeric(cc3), rownames(cc3))
    nz3_genes <- names(cc3_vals)[cc3_vals != 0 &
                                   names(cc3_vals) %in% outer_genes]

    cat("    M3 genes:", length(nz3_genes),
        "| lambda:", round(best_lambda_m3, 4),
        "| C:", round(c3, 3), "\n")

    for (g in nz3_genes) {
      prev_n <- if (g %in% names(selection_counts_m3)) selection_counts_m3[[g]] else 0L
      prev_c <- if (g %in% names(coef_sums_m3))        coef_sums_m3[[g]]        else 0
      selection_counts_m3[g] <- prev_n + 1L
      coef_sums_m3[g]        <- prev_c + cc3_vals[g]
    }

    c_model2[fit_i] <- c2
    c_model3[fit_i] <- c3

    fold_log[[fit_i]] <- list(
      rep        = rep_i,
      fold       = k,
      n_union    = length(union_genes),
      n_outer    = length(outer_genes),
      n_lasso_m2 = length(nz2),
      n_lasso_m3 = length(nz3_genes),
      c_model2   = c2,
      c_model3   = c3
    )
  }
}

fold_summary_cox <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fold_log, as.data.frame))

saveRDS(
  list(
    c_model2            = c_model2,
    c_model3            = c_model3,
    fold_summary        = fold_summary_cox,
    selection_counts_m2 = selection_counts_m2,
    selection_counts_m3 = selection_counts_m3,
    coef_sums_m2        = coef_sums_m2,
    coef_sums_m3        = coef_sums_m3
  ),
  cox_rds_path
)

cox_results_ready <- TRUE
cat("Cox nested-CV complete; saved to", cox_rds_path, "\n")

}
compute_c <- function(lp, surv_time, surv_event) {
  ok <- !is.na(lp) & !is.na(surv_time) & !is.na(surv_event)
  lp <- lp[ok]; surv_time <- surv_time[ok]; surv_event <- surv_event[ok]
  if (length(lp) < 2 || length(unique(lp)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  tryCatch({
    cfit <- concordance(Surv(surv_time, surv_event) ~ lp, reverse = TRUE)
    cfit$concordance
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("      [compute_c] error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    NA_real_
  })
}

rsf_results_ready <- rsf_cv_in_memory()

if (!rsf_results_ready && file.exists(rsf_rds_path)) {
  saved <- readRDS(rsf_rds_path)
  c_rsf_genes          <- saved$c_rsf_genes
  c_rsf_combined       <- saved$c_rsf_combined
  fold_summary_rsf     <- saved$fold_summary
  vimp_counts_genes    <- saved$vimp_counts_genes
  vimp_counts_combined <- saved$vimp_counts_combined
  vimp_sums_genes      <- saved$vimp_sums_genes
  vimp_sums_combined   <- saved$vimp_sums_combined
  rsf_results_ready    <- TRUE
  cat("RSF nested-CV results loaded from", rsf_rds_path, "\n")
} else if (rsf_results_ready) {
  cat("RSF nested-CV results already in memory; skipping recompute.\n")
}
if (!rsf_results_ready) {
  c_rsf_genes    <- numeric(n_outer_total)
  c_rsf_combined <- numeric(n_outer_total)

  fold_log <- vector("list", n_outer_total)
  fit_i    <- 0L

  vimp_counts_genes    <- integer(0)
  vimp_sums_genes      <- numeric(0)
  vimp_counts_combined <- integer(0)
  vimp_sums_combined   <- numeric(0)
}
# Random Survival Forest nested CV.
# RSF-Gene uses gene-expression features only; RSF-Combined adds the
# six histopathological variables. Inner CV picks ntree from {500, 1000}.
# Skips the loop when results are already in memory or in rsf_rds_path.

if (rsf_results_ready) {
  cat("Skipping RSF nested-CV loop (using saved results).\n")
} else {

for (rep_i in seq_len(n_outer_repeats)) {

  cat("=== Repeat", rep_i, "===\n")

  outer_folds <- make_stratified_folds(
    df_erpos_endo$ovrallSurvEvent,
    n_outer_folds,
    seed = 2000 + rep_i
  )

  for (k in seq_len(n_outer_folds)) {

    fit_i  <- fit_i + 1L
    tr_idx <- which(outer_folds != k)
    te_idx <- which(outer_folds == k)

    train_df   <- df_erpos_endo[tr_idx, ]
    test_df    <- df_erpos_endo[te_idx, ]
    expr_tr    <- expr_endo[, tr_idx, drop = FALSE]
    expr_te    <- expr_endo[, te_idx, drop = FALSE]

    cat("  Fold", k,
        "| train:", length(tr_idx),
        "| test:",  length(te_idx), "\n")

    inner_folds <- make_stratified_folds(
      train_df$ovrallSurvEvent,
      n_inner_folds,
      seed = 5000 + 100 * rep_i + k
    )

    candidate_genes_inner <- vector("list", n_inner_folds)

    for (ik in seq_len(n_inner_folds)) {
      itr_idx   <- which(inner_folds != ik)
      expr_itr  <- expr_tr[, itr_idx, drop = FALSE]
      event_itr <- train_df$ovrallSurvEvent[itr_idx]
      candidate_genes_inner[[ik]] <- select_genes_limma(
        expr_itr, event_itr, var_thresh, pval_thresh
      )
    }

    union_genes <- unique(unlist(candidate_genes_inner))
    union_genes <- union_genes[nchar(union_genes) > 0]

    cat("    Inner union genes:", length(union_genes), "\n")

    if (length(union_genes) < 2) {
      cat("    Too few genes, skipping RSF models\n")
      c_rsf_genes[fit_i]    <- NA_real_
      c_rsf_combined[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      next
    }

    ntree_candidates <- c(500, 1000)
    inner_c_by_ntree <- numeric(length(ntree_candidates))

    for (nt_i in seq_along(ntree_candidates)) {
      nt <- ntree_candidates[nt_i]
      inner_c_vals <- numeric(n_inner_folds)

      for (ik in seq_len(n_inner_folds)) {
        itr_idx <- which(inner_folds != ik)
        ite_idx <- which(inner_folds == ik)

        x_itr <- as.data.frame(t(expr_tr[union_genes, itr_idx, drop = FALSE]))
        x_itr[] <- lapply(x_itr, as.numeric)
        x_itr$time  <- train_df$ovrallSurvDays[itr_idx]
        x_itr$event <- train_df$ovrallSurvEvent[itr_idx]

        x_ite <- as.data.frame(t(expr_tr[union_genes, ite_idx, drop = FALSE]))
        x_ite[] <- lapply(x_ite, as.numeric)

        rsf_inner <- rfsrc(
          Surv(time, event) ~ .,
          data       = x_itr,
          ntree      = nt,
          nodesize   = 15,
          importance = FALSE,
          seed       = 42
        )

        pred_inner <- predict(rsf_inner, newdata = x_ite)
        inner_c_vals[ik] <- compute_c(
          pred_inner$predicted,
          train_df$ovrallSurvDays[ite_idx],
          train_df$ovrallSurvEvent[ite_idx]
        )
      }
      inner_c_by_ntree[nt_i] <- mean(inner_c_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
    }

    best_ntree <- ntree_candidates[which.max(inner_c_by_ntree)]
    cat("    Best ntree:", best_ntree, "\n")

    outer_genes <- select_genes_limma(
      expr_tr, train_df$ovrallSurvEvent,
      var_thresh, pval_thresh
    )

    cat("    Outer DGE genes:", length(outer_genes), "\n")

    if (length(outer_genes) < 2) {
      cat("    Too few outer genes, skipping\n")
      c_rsf_genes[fit_i]    <- NA_real_
      c_rsf_combined[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      next
    }

    x_tr_genes <- as.data.frame(t(expr_tr[outer_genes, , drop = FALSE]))
    x_tr_genes[] <- lapply(x_tr_genes, as.numeric)
    x_tr_genes$time  <- train_df$ovrallSurvDays
    x_tr_genes$event <- train_df$ovrallSurvEvent

    x_te_genes <- as.data.frame(t(expr_te[outer_genes, , drop = FALSE]))
    x_te_genes[] <- lapply(x_te_genes, as.numeric)

    rsf_genes <- rfsrc(
      Surv(time, event) ~ .,
      data       = x_tr_genes,
      ntree      = best_ntree,
      nodesize   = 15,
      importance = TRUE,
      seed       = 42
    )

    pred_genes <- predict(rsf_genes, newdata = x_te_genes)

    c_g <- compute_c(
      pred_genes$predicted,
      test_df$ovrallSurvDays,
      test_df$ovrallSurvEvent
    )

    vimp_g <- rsf_genes$importance
    top_genes_g <- names(sort(vimp_g[vimp_g > 0], decreasing = TRUE))

    cat("    RSF-Genes top features:", min(length(top_genes_g), 10),
        "| ntree:", best_ntree,
        "| C:", round(c_g, 3), "\n")

    for (g in top_genes_g) {
      prev_n <- if (g %in% names(vimp_counts_genes)) vimp_counts_genes[[g]] else 0L
      prev_c <- if (g %in% names(vimp_sums_genes))   vimp_sums_genes[[g]]   else 0
      vimp_counts_genes[g] <- prev_n + 1L
      vimp_sums_genes[g]   <- prev_c + vimp_g[g]
    }

    nhg_levels <- levels(as.factor(df_erpos_endo$nhg))

    x_tr_combined <- as.data.frame(t(expr_tr[outer_genes, , drop = FALSE]))
    x_tr_combined[] <- lapply(x_tr_combined, as.numeric)
    x_tr_combined$nhg              <- as.numeric(factor(train_df$nhg, levels = nhg_levels))
    x_tr_combined$pgr_Status       <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(train_df$pgr_Status)))
    x_tr_combined$her2_Status      <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(train_df$her2_Status)))
    x_tr_combined$tumor_size       <- as.numeric(train_df$tumor_size)
    x_tr_combined$ageAtDx          <- as.numeric(train_df$ageAtDx)
    x_tr_combined$lymphNode_binary <- as.numeric(train_df$lymphNode_binary)
    x_tr_combined$pgr_Status[is.na(x_tr_combined$pgr_Status)]   <- 1
    x_tr_combined$her2_Status[is.na(x_tr_combined$her2_Status)] <- 0
    x_tr_combined$time             <- train_df$ovrallSurvDays
    x_tr_combined$event            <- train_df$ovrallSurvEvent

    x_te_combined <- as.data.frame(t(expr_te[outer_genes, , drop = FALSE]))
    x_te_combined[] <- lapply(x_te_combined, as.numeric)
    x_te_combined$nhg              <- as.numeric(factor(test_df$nhg, levels = nhg_levels))
    x_te_combined$pgr_Status       <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(test_df$pgr_Status)))
    x_te_combined$her2_Status      <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(test_df$her2_Status)))
    x_te_combined$tumor_size       <- as.numeric(test_df$tumor_size)
    x_te_combined$ageAtDx          <- as.numeric(test_df$ageAtDx)
    x_te_combined$lymphNode_binary <- as.numeric(test_df$lymphNode_binary)
    x_te_combined$pgr_Status[is.na(x_te_combined$pgr_Status)]   <- 1
    x_te_combined$her2_Status[is.na(x_te_combined$her2_Status)] <- 0

    rsf_combined <- rfsrc(
      Surv(time, event) ~ .,
      data       = x_tr_combined,
      ntree      = best_ntree,
      nodesize   = 15,
      importance = TRUE,
      seed       = 42
    )

    pred_combined <- tryCatch(
      predict(rsf_combined, newdata = x_te_combined),
      error = function(e) {
        cat("      [predict RSF-combined] error:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
        NULL
      }
    )

    if (is.null(pred_combined)) {
      c_rsf_combined[fit_i] <- NA_real_
      cat("    RSF-Combined: predict failed, skipping\n")
    } else {
      cat("      [debug] pred range:", range(pred_combined$predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
          "| NAs:", sum(is.na(pred_combined$predicted)), "\n")
    }

    c_c <- if (!is.null(pred_combined)) {
      compute_c(
        pred_combined$predicted,
        test_df$ovrallSurvDays,
        test_df$ovrallSurvEvent
      )
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }

    vimp_c <- rsf_combined$importance
    top_features_c <- names(sort(vimp_c[vimp_c > 0], decreasing = TRUE))

    cat("    RSF-Combined top features:", min(length(top_features_c), 10),
        "| ntree:", best_ntree,
        "| C:", round(c_c, 3), "\n")

    for (g in top_features_c) {
      prev_n <- if (g %in% names(vimp_counts_combined)) vimp_counts_combined[[g]] else 0L
      prev_c <- if (g %in% names(vimp_sums_combined))   vimp_sums_combined[[g]]   else 0
      vimp_counts_combined[g] <- prev_n + 1L
      vimp_sums_combined[g]   <- prev_c + vimp_c[g]
    }

    c_rsf_genes[fit_i]    <- c_g
    c_rsf_combined[fit_i] <- c_c

    fold_log[[fit_i]] <- list(
      rep          = rep_i,
      fold         = k,
      n_union      = length(union_genes),
      n_outer      = length(outer_genes),
      best_ntree   = best_ntree,
      n_vimp_genes = length(top_genes_g),
      n_vimp_comb  = length(top_features_c),
      c_rsf_genes  = c_g,
      c_rsf_comb   = c_c
    )
  }
}

fold_summary_rsf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(fold_log, as.data.frame))

saveRDS(
  list(
    c_rsf_genes          = c_rsf_genes,
    c_rsf_combined       = c_rsf_combined,
    fold_summary         = fold_summary_rsf,
    vimp_counts_genes    = vimp_counts_genes,
    vimp_counts_combined = vimp_counts_combined,
    vimp_sums_genes      = vimp_sums_genes,
    vimp_sums_combined   = vimp_sums_combined
  ),
  rsf_rds_path
)

rsf_results_ready <- TRUE
cat("RSF nested-CV complete; saved to", rsf_rds_path, "\n")

}

4.5 Evaluation Strategy

The primary discrimination metric is Harrell’s C-statistic (Harrell et al., 1982), defined as the proportion of evaluable patient pairs in which the model correctly ranks the patient who died first as having a higher predicted risk score; 0.5 represents no discrimination beyond chance, 1.0 represents perfect discrimination. The C-statistic is the natural choice for Cox models because it evaluates what the model is optimising (ranking by hazard) rather than imposing an arbitrary classification threshold (Steyerberg et al., 2010). For Cox we compute it via survcomp::concordance.index (Noether’s method); for RSF we use survival::concordance with reverse = TRUE on the raw predicted mortality, matching standard RSF practice.

Pairwise model comparison uses a paired t-test on the 25 per-fold C-statistics within each model family, pairing fold-by-fold so that both members of a comparison see identical patients in each split. Pairing is essential because within-fold correlation in performance is substantial, and an unpaired test would discard most of the statistical power available.

Stability selection follows Meinshausen and Buhlmann (2010): a gene is declared “stable” if it receives a non-zero LASSO coefficient (or, for RSF, a positive variable importance) in a sufficient fraction of the 25 outer fits. The default threshold is 80%; for the final deployed gene panel, this is relaxed to 70% on the Cox-Combined results to balance parsimony with stability, as discussed in the Stable Gene Panel results below.

5 Results

5.1 Cross-Validated Discrimination

Figure 3 presents the per-fold C-statistic across all 25 outer fits for the four models. Two findings are immediate. First, combining histopathology with gene expression improves discrimination in both modelling families: Cox-Combined exceeds Cox-Gene at nearly every fold, and RSF-Combined exceeds RSF-Gene at nearly every fold. Second, Cox-LASSO outperforms RSF at the matching configuration: Cox-Gene exceeds RSF-Gene, and Cox-Combined exceeds RSF-Combined.

Figure 3. Per-fold Harrell C-statistic across 25 outer fits for the four candidate models (Cox-Gene, Cox-Combined, RSF-Gene, RSF-Combined). Both modelling families show a consistent gain from adding histopathological variables, and Cox-LASSO outperforms RSF at each matching configuration.

Table 1 summarises central tendency and spread. The combined Cox model achieves a mean C-statistic of 0.766 (SD 0.036, range 0.677 to 0.822), 0.071 higher than its gene-only counterpart (mean 0.695, SD 0.044, paired t-test p < 0.0001). The combined RSF model achieves a mean C-statistic of 0.716 (SD 0.052), 0.041 higher than its gene-only counterpart (mean 0.674, SD 0.047, paired p < 0.0001). All four sit above 0.5, and the combined models sit in the range commonly described as moderate-to-good discrimination in prognostic modelling literature (Hosmer and Lemeshow, 2000).

5.1.1 Comparative Assessment: Cox vs RSF

Cox-LASSO outperforms Random Survival Forest at both configurations, and by a comfortable margin (Cox-Gene minus RSF-Gene approximately +0.021 on the mean, Cox-Combined minus RSF-Combined approximately +0.050). This is informative: the semi-parametric, additive-on-the-log-hazard structure of Cox-LASSO is matched well to the signal in this cohort, and the additional flexibility of an ensemble of trees does not pay back its variance cost at the available sample size. Both families agree, however, on the qualitative conclusion that adding histopathological variables provides a statistically significant and clinically meaningful uplift over gene expression alone, which strengthens confidence that this gain is a property of the data rather than of one particular model class. On the basis of both discrimination and interpretability (Cox returns per-feature coefficients that can be audited and explained), Cox-Combined is retained as the deployment model.

5.2 Stable Gene Panel

Across the 25 outer fits, the Cox-Gene model selected a median of 102 genes per fold (IQR 76 to 115), while the Cox-Combined model selected fewer (median 79, IQR 56 to 92), consistent with the histopathological variables absorbing part of the survival signal. At the default 80% stability threshold, Cox-Gene yielded 14 stable genes and Cox-Combined yielded 9. Several genes appeared in both stable sets (notably VAV3, GREB1, KIRREL3, HV592909, DQ588543), suggesting they capture survival signal independent of whether clinical variables are present.

For the final deployed model the threshold on Cox-Combined was relaxed from 80% to 70%, yielding 11 genes: B3GNT7, VAV3, PCAT18, HV592909, DQ588543, DQ583069, GREB1, KIRREL3, NR6A1, HIST1H4J, and DQ577476. The relaxation trades a small amount of stability for sufficient coverage that the Shiny tool can elicit a single manageable CSV of 11 expression values from the user. GREB1 is a well-established estrogen-receptor signalling gene, providing biological face validity for the signature.

5.3 Final Deployed Model and Risk Stratification

Using the 11 stability-selected genes and the six histopathological variables, an unpenalised Cox proportional hazards model was refitted on all 2,512 patients. The resulting model achieved a C-statistic of 0.818 on the training cohort (somewhat optimistic relative to the nested CV estimate, as expected for a training-set C-statistic, but consistent with the rank order in Table 1). Predicted linear predictors were partitioned at the 33rd and 67th percentiles to define Low, Medium, and High risk tiers. The observed mortality rates within each tier are sharply separated: Low 1.2% (n = 838), Medium 4.9% (n = 837), High 20.2% (n = 837).

                    "HV592909", "DQ588543", "DQ583069",
                    "GREB1", "KIRREL3", "NR6A1",
                    "HIST1H4J", "DQ577476")

                    "nhg", "pgr_Status", "her2_Status",

)

                 df_erpos_endo$ovrallSurvEvent)

  as.formula(paste(
    "surv_all ~ nhg + pgr_Status + her2_Status +",

  event = df_erpos_endo$ovrallSurvEvent,
  tier  = tier3
)

  legend.title = "Risk tier",
  legend.labs  = c("Low", "Medium", "High"),

Figure 4. Kaplan-Meier overall survival curves for the three risk tiers (Low / Medium / High) defined by tertiles of the final Cox-Combined linear predictor on all 2,512 patients. The log-rank test gives p < 0.0001, and the observed mortality rates within each tier are 1.2 percent (Low), 4.9 percent (Medium), and 20.2 percent (High).

5.4 Shiny Risk Calculator

The final Cox-Combined model, the 11-gene panel, and the tertile cut-points are loaded by a Shiny web application (full source in Appendix). Clinicians enter the six histopathological variables and upload a CSV of expression values for the 11 stability-selected genes; the application returns a percentile rank within the training cohort, an assigned risk tier with the corresponding group-level death rate, personalised 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival estimates from the fitted Cox model, and the top three drivers pushing the patient’s risk up and down (computed from the per-feature contribution to the linear predictor relative to the cohort mean). The interface is positioned as decision support for pathologist-to-oncologist reporting rather than as a standalone diagnostic.

6 Discussion

6.1 Key Findings

The central finding is that histopathology and RNA-seq are complementary rather than substitutable for survival risk stratification in ER+ endocrine-treated breast cancer. In both Cox-LASSO and Random Survival Forest, the combined model significantly and consistently outperforms the gene-only model on the same outer folds (Cox: +0.071, RSF: +0.041, both p < 0.0001 paired). This rules out the possibility that the gain is an artefact of one particular model choice. The gene-expression signal alone delivers moderate discrimination (Cox-Gene mean C = 0.695), consistent with the EDA observation in Figure 1 that molecular vs histopathological ER discordance carries a real survival signal.

A second finding is that the parametric Cox model outperforms the more flexible RSF at both gene-only and combined configurations. This is not a universally expected result, and it suggests that the survival signal in SCAN-B at the available sample size is captured well by an additive linear predictor on the log-hazard, the extra flexibility of trees does not pay back its variance cost. This also reinforces the choice of Cox-LASSO for deployment: it provides per-feature interpretable coefficients that can be audited and explained, which is critical for clinical adoption.

The 11-gene panel includes GREB1, a well-characterised estrogen-receptor-signalling gene, alongside VAV3 and several less-characterised transcripts. Together with the six clinical features, this panel produces a three-tier output with sharply separated observed mortality (1.2% / 4.9% / 20.2%, Figure 4), which is the form most directly useful to a clinician deciding whether a patient warrants reassessment.

6.2 Limitations

Several limitations apply. First, the study population is a single Swedish cohort restricted to ER+ patients on endocrine therapy, so generalisation to ER-negative subtypes, alternative treatment regimens, or non-European populations is not established. Second, missing clinical values were imputed by mode or median, which is pragmatic but biases the cohort toward the modal patient. Third, Ki67 was excluded entirely due to its 54.8% missingness, removing a marker that is clinically informative in practice. Fourth, the relaxation of the stability threshold from 80% to 70% for the deployed gene panel means a small number of genes in the final panel have weaker selection support than the strictest interpretation of stability selection would require. Fifth, no external validation on an independent cohort (e.g. TCGA-BRCA or METABRIC) has been performed, and prospective use should not precede that step. Sixth, only overall survival was modelled, disease-free or breast-cancer-specific survival could give a slightly different ranking of features. Finally, the use of lambda.min rather than lambda.1se selects more features and may marginally increase overfitting risk, although the nested CV evaluation already accounts for this.

6.3 Future Work

The most important next step is external validation of the 11-gene Cox-Combined signature on an independent cohort such as TCGA-BRCA or METABRIC. Beyond that, three extensions are natural: incorporating disease-free survival as a secondary endpoint, broadening the population beyond ER+ endocrine-treated patients to include additional biomarker contexts (e.g. PgR and HER2 status as primary stratifiers), and probability calibration so that the Shiny tool can return calibrated absolute survival probabilities at fixed horizons rather than relative tier membership alone.

7 Conclusion

Combining histopathology with RNA-seq gene expression delivers consistent and statistically significant improvements in survival risk stratification over gene expression alone in ER+ endocrine-treated breast cancer. This result holds in both Cox-LASSO and Random Survival Forest, with Cox-LASSO selected as the deployment model on the grounds of interpretability and superior discrimination at this sample size. The resulting 11-gene panel together with six clinical variables yields three-tier risk groups with mortality rates of 1.2%, 4.9%, and 20.2%, and is operationalised in a Shiny application designed to fit into a pathologist-to-oncologist reporting workflow rather than to replace existing clinical judgement.

10.1 A.1 Cox Results Summary

This summary uses the variables produced by the cox-loop chunk in the Methods section. If that chunk has not yet been run (or its cache has been invalidated) the summary is skipped with a clear message rather than throwing a file-not-found error.

cox_rds <- "./models/cox_m2_m3_final.rds"

if (!file.exists(cox_rds)) {
  cat("Cox nested-CV results not available yet.\n",
      "Run the 'cox-loop' chunk in the Methods section first.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  saved <- readRDS(cox_rds)

  c_m2          <- saved$c_model2
  c_m3          <- saved$c_model3
  fold_sum_cox  <- saved$fold_summary
  n_outer_total <- length(c_m2)

  cat(sprintf("\n=== Cox RESULTS (%d outer fits) ===\n\n", n_outer_total))

  cat(sprintf(
    "Cox-Gene (LASSO, lambda.min):\n  Mean C = %.3f (SD = %.3f, range = %.3f to %.3f)\n\n",
    mean(c_m2, na.rm = TRUE), sd(c_m2, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(c_m2, na.rm = TRUE),  max(c_m2, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))

  cat(sprintf(
    "Cox-Combined (LASSO, lambda.min):\n  Mean C = %.3f (SD = %.3f, range = %.3f to %.3f)\n\n",
    mean(c_m3, na.rm = TRUE), sd(c_m3, na.rm = TRUE),
    min(c_m3, na.rm = TRUE),  max(c_m3, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))

  cat(sprintf("Cox-Gene genes selected: median = %.0f (IQR %.0f to %.0f)\n",
    median(fold_sum_cox$n_lasso_m2, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(fold_sum_cox$n_lasso_m2, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(fold_sum_cox$n_lasso_m2, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))
  cat(sprintf("Cox-Combined genes selected: median = %.0f (IQR %.0f to %.0f)\n\n",
    median(fold_sum_cox$n_lasso_m3, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(fold_sum_cox$n_lasso_m3, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    quantile(fold_sum_cox$n_lasso_m3, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))

  cat("=== PAIRED T-TEST (Cox) ===\n\n")
  diff_cox  <- c_m3 - c_m2
  ttest_cox <- t.test(c_m3, c_m2, paired = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf(
    "Cox-Combined vs Cox-Gene:\n  Mean diff = %+.3f (SD = %.3f), p = %.4f\n\n",
    mean(diff_cox, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd(diff_cox,   na.rm = TRUE),
    ttest_cox$p.value
  ))

  stab_thresh <- 0.80

  report_stability <- function(sel_counts, coef_sums_vec, label) {
    if (length(sel_counts) == 0) {
      cat(label, ": no genes selected\n\n")
      return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    sel_freq <- sort(sel_counts / n_outer_total, decreasing = TRUE)
    stable   <- names(sel_freq)[sel_freq >= stab_thresh]
    cat(sprintf("%s:\n  Genes selected at least once: %d\n", label, length(sel_freq)))
    cat(sprintf("  Stable genes (>= 80%%): %d\n\n", length(stable)))
    if (length(stable) > 0) {
      mean_coef <- coef_sums_vec[stable] / pmax(sel_counts[stable], 1L)
      sig_df <- data.frame(
        gene           = stable,
        selection_freq = round(sel_freq[stable], 3),
        mean_coef      = round(as.numeric(mean_coef), 4),
        row.names      = NULL
      )
      sig_df <- sig_df[order(-sig_df$selection_freq, -abs(sig_df$mean_coef)), ]
      print(sig_df, row.names = FALSE)
      cat("\n")
    }
    invisible(stable)
  }

  report_stability(saved$selection_counts_m2, saved$coef_sums_m2,
                   "Cox-Gene (LASSO)")
  report_stability(saved$selection_counts_m3, saved$coef_sums_m3,
                   "Cox-Combined (LASSO)")
}

10.3 A.3 Shiny Application Source

The deployed Shiny application loads the final Cox-Combined model and the tertile cut-points and presents the risk-stratification interface described in the Shiny Risk Calculator subsection of Results. The full source is reproduced below for reference (chunk option eval = FALSE, so it does not run during knit). When you launch it manually it expects the following RDS files in ./models/: cox3_final.rds, cuts3.rds, stable_genes_m3.rds (written by the final-refit chunk), and df_erpos_endo.rds, expr_endo.rds (written by the data-load chunk). Run those chunks first if you want to run the app interactively.

library(shiny)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(shinyjs)



cox3_final      <- readRDS("./models/cox3_final.rds")
cuts3           <- readRDS("./models/cuts3.rds")
stable_genes_m3 <- readRDS("./models/stable_genes_m3.rds")
df_erpos_endo   <- readRDS("./models/df_erpos_endo.rds")
expr_endo       <- readRDS("./models/expr_endo.rds")

death_rates <- c(Low = 1.2, Medium = 4.9, High = 20.2)
tier_ns     <- c(Low = 838, Medium = 837, High = 837)
c_stat      <- 0.818

get_tier <- function(score, cuts) {
  if (score <= cuts[1]) "Low"
  else if (score <= cuts[2]) "Medium"
  else "High"
}



tier_colour <- function(tier) switch(tier, Low="#1B7A4A", Medium="#C47A00", High="#B02020")
tier_bg     <- function(tier) switch(tier, Low="#EAF5EE", Medium="#FEF6E4", High="#FDECEC")
ordinal <- function(n) {
  s <- ifelse(n %in% c(11,12,13), "th",
       ifelse(n%%10==1,"st", ifelse(n%%10==2,"nd", ifelse(n%%10==3,"rd","th"))))
  paste0(n, s)
}

# Pre-compute KM medians per tier
all_risk3 <- predict(cox3_final, type = "lp")
tier_all  <- cut(all_risk3, breaks = c(-Inf, cuts3, Inf),
                 labels = c("Low","Medium","High"))
km_data <- data.frame(
  time  = df_erpos_endo$ovrallSurvDays,
  event = df_erpos_endo$ovrallSurvEvent,
  tier  = tier_all
)
km_medians <- sapply(c("Low","Medium","High"), function(t) {
  sub <- km_data[km_data$tier == t, ]
  fit <- survfit(Surv(time, event) ~ 1, data = sub)
  med <- summary(fit)$table["median"]
  if (is.na(med)) max(sub$time[sub$event==0], na.rm=TRUE) else med
})

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$clear_csv, {
  reset("rna_csv")
    })
  
  output$has_rna <- reactive({
  !is.null(input$rna_csv) && !is.null(input$rna_csv$datapath)
  })
  outputOptions(output, "has_rna", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
  
  results <- eventReactive(input$run, {

    gene_vals <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(stable_genes_m3)), stable_genes_m3)
    has_rna   <- FALSE

    if (!is.null(input$rna_csv) && !is.null(input$rna_csv$datapath)) {
      tryCatch({
        expr_csv <- read.csv(input$rna_csv$datapath, row.names=1, check.names=FALSE)
        missing  <- setdiff(stable_genes_m3, colnames(expr_csv))
        if (ncol(expr_csv) != length(stable_genes_m3)) {
          showNotification(paste0("CSV must have exactly ",length(stable_genes_m3),
                                  " gene columns. Found ",ncol(expr_csv),"."),
                           type="error", duration=8)
        } else if (length(missing) > 0) {
          showNotification(paste0("Missing genes: ",paste(missing,collapse=", ")),
                           type="error", duration=8)
        } else {
          gene_vals <- as.numeric(expr_csv[1, stable_genes_m3])
          names(gene_vals) <- stable_genes_m3
          has_rna <- TRUE
        }
      }, error=function(e) showNotification("Could not read CSV.",type="error",duration=8))
    }

    coefs    <- coef(cox3_final)
    means    <- cox3_final$means
    nhg_val  <- as.integer(input$nhg)
    pgr_val  <- as.integer(input$pgr)
    her2_val <- as.integer(input$her2)

    new_vec <- c(
      nhgG2=as.numeric(nhg_val==2), nhgG3=as.numeric(nhg_val==3), nhgNA=0,
      pgr_Status1=as.numeric(pgr_val==1), pgr_StatusNA=0,
      her2_Status1=as.numeric(her2_val==1), her2_StatusNA=0,
      tumor_size=as.numeric(input$tumor_size),
      ageAtDx=as.numeric(input$age),
      lymphNode_binary=as.numeric(input$lymph_node)
    )
    gene_input <- if (has_rna) gene_vals[stable_genes_m3] else means[stable_genes_m3]
    new_vec    <- c(new_vec, gene_input)

    risk <- tryCatch(
      sum(coefs * (new_vec[names(coefs)] - means[names(coefs)]), na.rm=TRUE),
      error=function(e) NA_real_
    )

    tier     <- if (!is.na(risk)) get_tier(risk, cuts3) else NA_character_
    all_risk <- predict(cox3_final, type="lp")
    pct      <- if (!is.na(risk)) round(mean(all_risk <= risk)*100) else NA

    contrib <- coefs * (new_vec[names(coefs)] - means[names(coefs)])
    contrib  <- contrib[!is.na(contrib)]

    # Personalised survival probabilities
    surv_1yr <- surv_3yr <- surv_5yr <- NA
    tryCatch({
      nhg_str <- switch(as.character(as.integer(input$nhg)),
                        "1" = "G1", "2" = "G2", "3" = "G3", "G1")

      nd <- data.frame(
        nhg              = nhg_str,
        pgr_Status       = as.character(as.integer(input$pgr)),
        her2_Status      = as.character(as.integer(input$her2)),
        tumor_size       = as.numeric(input$tumor_size),
        ageAtDx          = as.numeric(input$age),
        lymphNode_binary = as.numeric(input$lymph_node),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      gene_input <- if (has_rna) gene_vals[stable_genes_m3] else means[stable_genes_m3]
      for (g in stable_genes_m3) nd[[g]] <- gene_input[g]

      fit_surv  <- survfit(cox3_final, newdata = nd)
      s_summary <- summary(fit_surv, times = c(365, 1095, 1826))
      sp        <- s_summary$surv
      if (length(sp) >= 1) surv_1yr <- round(sp[1]*100, 1)
      if (length(sp) >= 2) surv_3yr <- round(sp[2]*100, 1)
      if (length(sp) >= 3) surv_5yr <- round(sp[3]*100, 1)
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    list(risk=risk, tier=tier, pct=pct,
         has_rna=has_rna, gene_vals=gene_vals, contrib=contrib,
         surv_1yr=surv_1yr, surv_3yr=surv_3yr, surv_5yr=surv_5yr)
  })

  output$gauge <- renderPlot({
    res <- results()
    if (is.na(res$tier)) return(NULL)
    pct         <- res$pct
    gauge_angle <- pi - (pct/100)*pi
    theta_full  <- seq(pi, 0, length.out=300)
    par(mar=c(1.5,1,1,1), bg="white")
    plot(0,0,type="n",xlim=c(-1.4,1.4),ylim=c(-0.4,1.3),asp=1,axes=FALSE,xlab="",ylab="")
    lines(cos(theta_full),sin(theta_full),lwd=20,col="#EEEBE6")
    for (z in list(list(from=pi,to=pi*2/3,col="#1B7A4A"),
                   list(from=pi*2/3,to=pi*1/3,col="#C47A00"),
                   list(from=pi*1/3,to=0,col="#B02020"))) {
      th <- seq(z$from,z$to,length.out=80)
      lines(cos(th),sin(th),lwd=20,col=z$col)
    }
    nx <- cos(gauge_angle)*0.70; ny <- sin(gauge_angle)*0.70
    segments(0,0,nx,ny,lwd=3,col="#1C1C1C",lend=1)
    points(0,0,pch=21,bg="#1C1C1C",col="white",cex=2.5,lwd=2)
    text(-1.22,0.20,"LOW",cex=0.70,col="#1B7A4A",font=2)
    text(0,1.18,"MEDIUM",cex=0.70,col="#C47A00",font=2)
    text(1.22,0.20,"HIGH",cex=0.70,col="#B02020",font=2)
    text(0,-0.26,paste0(ordinal(pct)," percentile"),cex=0.80,col="#777")
  }, bg="white")

  output$risk_label <- renderUI({
    res    <- results()
    if (is.na(res$tier)) return(NULL)
    col    <- tier_colour(res$tier)
    bg_col <- tier_bg(res$tier)
    dr     <- death_rates[res$tier]
    med    <- km_medians[res$tier]

    interp <- switch(res$tier,
      Low    = "Low risk patients have a favourable prognosis. Standard endocrine therapy follow-up is appropriate.",
      Medium = "Intermediate risk. Enhanced monitoring or clinical discussion may be warranted.",
      High   = "High risk of mortality. Intensified treatment strategy or multidisciplinary review is recommended."
    )
    
  
    surv_1yr <- res$surv_1yr
    surv_3yr <- res$surv_3yr
    surv_5yr <- res$surv_5yr

    surv_row <- function(label, val) {
      div(style=paste0("display:flex;justify-content:space-between;",
                       "padding:7px 0;border-bottom:1px solid #F5F2EE;font-size:13px;"),
        span(style="color:#777;", label),
        span(style=paste0("font-weight:600;color:",col),
             if (is.na(val)) "-" else paste0(val,"%"))
      )
    }

    div(style="padding:8px 0;",
      div(style=paste0("font-size:32px;font-weight:700;color:",col,
                       ";letter-spacing:1px;margin-bottom:8px;"),
          toupper(res$tier)," RISK"),
      div(style=paste0("display:inline-block;padding:5px 14px;border-radius:16px;",
                       "background:",bg_col,";color:",col,
                       ";font-size:13px;font-weight:500;",
                       "border:1px solid ",col,"33;margin-bottom:14px;"),
          paste0(dr,"% group death rate")),
      div(style="margin-bottom:14px;",
        div(style="font-size:10px;font-weight:600;letter-spacing:1.5px;
                   text-transform:uppercase;color:#AAA;margin-bottom:4px;",
            "Personalised Survival Estimates"),
        surv_row("1-year survival", surv_1yr),
        surv_row("3-year survival", surv_3yr),
        surv_row("5-year survival", surv_5yr)
      ),
      div(style="font-size:13px;color:#444;line-height:1.6;margin-bottom:8px;", interp)
    )
  })

  output$tier_bar <- renderUI({
    res <- results()
    if (is.na(res$tier)) return(NULL)
    pt   <- res$tier
    cols <- c(Low="#1B7A4A",Medium="#C47A00",High="#B02020")
    bgs  <- c(Low="#EAF5EE",Medium="#FEF6E4",High="#FDECEC")
    segs <- lapply(c("Low","Medium","High"), function(t) {
      act <- t == pt
      div(class=paste("tier-seg",if(act)"active" else ""),
          style=paste0("background:",if(act)bgs[t] else "#F5F2EE",";",
                       "border:",if(act)paste0("2px solid ",cols[t]) else "1px solid #E4E0D8",";",
                       "color:",if(act)cols[t] else "#AAA",";"),
        div(style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;",toupper(t)),
        div(style=paste0("font-size:16px;font-weight:700;",
                         if(act)paste0("color:",cols[t]) else ""),
          paste0(death_rates[t], "% death risk"))
      )
    })
    div(
      div(style="font-size:12px;color:#888;margin-bottom:8px;",
          HTML(paste0("This patient is in the <strong>", pt, "</strong> risk group."))),
      div(class="tier-bar-wrap", segs)
    )
  })

  output$drivers_panel <- renderUI({
    res <- results()
    if (is.na(res$tier)) return(NULL)
    col    <- tier_colour(res$tier)
    contrib <- res$contrib
    label_map <- c(
      nhgG2="NHG Grade 2", nhgG3="NHG Grade 3",
      pgr_Status1="PgR Positive", her2_Status1="HER2 Positive",
      tumor_size="Tumour Size", ageAtDx="Age at Diagnosis",
      lymphNode_binary="Lymph Node Positive",
      B3GNT7="B3GNT7", VAV3="VAV3", PCAT18="PCAT18",
      HV592909="HV592909", DQ588543="DQ588543", DQ583069="DQ583069",
      GREB1="GREB1", KIRREL3="KIRREL3", NR6A1="NR6A1",
      HIST1H4J="HIST1H4J", DQ577476="DQ577476"
    )
    
    df_c <- data.frame(variable = names(contrib), 
                       contribution = as.numeric(contrib),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      mutate(label = ifelse(variable %in% names(label_map), 
                            label_map[variable], variable)) %>%
      filter(!variable %in% c("nhgNA", "pgr_StatusNA", "her2_StatusNA"))
    
    risk_d <- df_c %>% arrange(desc(contribution)) %>% head(3)
    prot_d <- df_c %>% arrange(contribution)        %>% head(3)

    make_tags <- function(drivers, col, bg, arrow) {
      if (nrow(drivers)==0) return(div(style="color:#AAA;font-size:12px;","None"))
      div(class="driver-row",
        lapply(seq_len(nrow(drivers)), function(i)
          div(class="driver-tag",
              style=paste0("background:",bg,";color:",col,";border:1px solid ",col,"33;"),
            span(arrow), span(drivers$label[i]))))
    }
    div(
          div(style="margin-bottom:14px;",
            div(style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:#B02020;","INCREASING RISK"),
            div(style="margin-top:6px;",make_tags(risk_d,"#B02020","#FDECEC","↑"))
          ),
          div(
            div(style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;color:#1B7A4A;","DECREASING RISK"),
            div(style="margin-top:6px;",make_tags(prot_d,"#1B7A4A","#EAF5EE","↓"))
        )
    )
  })
}
shinyApp(ui=ui, server=server)
